findings.where: Hero, the headline "Mark M. Moseley, infrastructure advisor" and the line under it (desktop and phone first screen)
findings.fault: The page's strongest element is a name and job title, and the line under it describes Mark in the third person. The brief asks for a headline in Mark's own words: one strong line in his voice. The article specimen just below speaks in his first person ("a client … asked me"), so the homepage sounds like a directory entry while the blog sounds like the man. Squinting, the loudest thing on the first screen carries no judgement or point of view, only a label.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the founder. Client values 3 and 6 and the v5 card's carry-over ask for Mark seen and heard in his own words, with one confident line. A development-bank officer arriving from LinkedIn already knows his name and title, so the headline tells them nothing new about why to write to him.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the principle words "precise, light, quick", the easing note "brisk out of rest", and the chosen element (the heading's two lines)
findings.fault: The motion principles this tile hands to the animation round (#9) are about speed and UI snap: "quick" twice, a brisk start, a 580 ms total for two text lines. The brief's client values ask for calm first (one quiet moment before anything asks for attention) and smooth animation built around the aqueduct. The v5 card makes the mark the only picture. The sketch animates a heading, not the mark, so it shows nothing about how the aqueduct and logo should move in this direction.
findings.who_objects: The founder and the animation round. The animation round must draw inside these principles, and "quick" contradicts the calm, smooth character Mark asked for (§6, LoveFrom's "smooth animation built around the aqueduct"). Mark would see a snappy UI reveal where he expected the aqueduct being built.

findings.where: Hero, the supporting line "Advice on infrastructure projects and the laws that enable them … Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience"
findings.fault: In five seconds a visitor learns what Mark does, but not who it is for or where he works. Nothing names governments, development agencies or regions. The proof offered last is a size claim ("Over 40 years"), not something checkable. The World Bank role in the same line is the checkable fact, and the year count dilutes it into a boast.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank and agency staff, the audience in §1. They select advisors by project kind and region, and they want to see that Mark has done work for bodies like theirs (first-visit trust items 2 and 6, and "Feel the CV": no size words). Mark's own value 6 also asks for no boasts.
